title: `Core\Math::abs` is typed `int|float|decimal` whatever it is given, so its result cannot be stored in the argument's own type without `as`.
text: `ABS_DOC` and `nvs_core_math_abs`'s doc both say the result is in `$n`'s own type, and at run time it is, but the registry row declares `params: [CoreTy::Union(NUMBER)]` and `return_ty: CoreTy::Union(NUMBER)`, so the checker sees the whole union at every call. `decimal $owed = Core\Math::abs($balance);` fails with `E0401` (expected `decimal`, found `int|float|decimal`), and `int $sum = $sum + Core\Math::abs($x);` fails with found `mixed`, so every arithmetic use needs `as`. `min`, `max` and `clamp` return their argument's type through `CoreTy::Var("T")`, but an unbounded variable would let `abs("x")` compile and throw at run time, which gives up the compile-time refusal the union provides. The fix is a type variable bounded by a union, which `nvs_types::core_lib::lower` interns and the unifier checks after binding. That is a new `CoreTy` shape reaching `nvs-types`, `nvs-ir`'s call lowering, `nvs meta` and the LSP stubs, and it is a design question rather than a slice. `docs/examples/core/Math/abs/03-showing-a-balance-in-words.nvs` is marked `known-gap` for this entry; its attack and its bench convert with `as int` today.
